questions.q:
A: Entropy of a perfect crystalline solid at absolute zero approaches zero.
B: For spontaneity of a reaction, T$\Delta$S > $\Delta$H.
Among the two statements given above, identify the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement A is the third law of thermodynamics (true); for spontaneity $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$, i.e. $T\Delta S > \Delta H$, so B is also true.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement for a thermodynamic system?
options: The internal energy changes in all processes
Internal energy and entropy are state functions
The work done in an adiabatic process is always zero
questions.explanation: Internal energy and entropy are both state functions (path-independent); work and heat are path functions, and adiabatic work need not be zero.

questions.q: A gas can be taken from A to B via two different paths ACB and ADB. When path ACB is used, 60J of heat flows into the system and 30J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used, work done by the system is 10J. The heat flow into the system in path ADB is [P-V diagram: rectangle with A at bottom-left, C at top-left, B at top-right, D at bottom-right]
questions.explanation: $\Delta U$ is path-independent: along ACB, $\Delta U = q - w = 60 - 30 = 30$ J. Along ADB, $q = \Delta U + w = 30 + 10 = 40$ J.

questions.q: Given below are two statements. Statement-I: Adiabatic work done is positive when work is done on the system and internal energy of the system increases. Statement-II: No work is done during free expansion of an ideal gas. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
questions.explanation: By the IUPAC sign convention, work done on the system is positive and raises internal energy (Statement-I true); free expansion occurs against zero external pressure, so no work is done (Statement-II true).

questions.q: Which one of the following reactions has $\Delta H = \Delta U$?
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Delta U$ when the change in the number of gaseous moles is zero; only 2HI(g)⇌H$_2$(g)+I$_2$(g) has $\Delta n_g = 2-2 = 0$.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect statements among the following: (a) All enthalpies of fusion are positive. (b) The magnitude of enthalpy change does not depend on the strength of the intermolecular interactions in the substance undergoing phase transformations. (c) When a chemical reaction is reversed, the value of $\Delta_rH^\circ$ is reversed in sign. (d) The change in enthalpy is dependent of path between initial state (reactants) and final state (products) (e) For most of the ionic compounds, $\Delta_{sol}H^\circ$ is negative.
questions.explanation: Statement (b) is false because enthalpy change does depend on the strength of intermolecular forces; (d) is false because enthalpy is a state function, independent of path; (e) is false since the enthalpy of solution of many ionic compounds is actually positive; so b, d and e are incorrect.

questions.q: From the diagram A $\xrightarrow{\Delta H_1=+10J}$ 2B $\xrightarrow{\Delta H_2=+25J}$ C. $\Delta_r H$ for the reaction C$\rightarrow$A is:
questions.explanation: A$\rightarrow$C via B has $\Delta H = \Delta H_1+\Delta H_2 = 35$ J, so the reverse reaction C$\rightarrow$A has $\Delta H = -35$ J.

questions.q: Lattice enthalpy for NaCl is + 788 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta$H$^\circ_{Hyd}$ = -784 kJ mol$^{-1}$. Enthalpy of solution of NaCl is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H_{solution} = \Delta H_{lattice} + \Delta H_{hydration} = 788 + (-784) = +4\ kJ\,mol^{-1}$.

questions.q: The work done when 2 moles of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from a volume of 1 L to 10 L at 300 K is (R = 0.0083 kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: W = nRT ln(V$_2$/V$_1$) = 2 $\times$ 0.0083 $\times$ 300 $\times$ ln 10 $\approx$ 4.98 $\times$ 2.303 $\approx$ 11.5 kJ.

questions.q: When the same quantity of heat is absorbed by a system at two different temperatures T$_1$ and T$_2$, such that T$_1$ > T$_2$, the changes in entropies are $\Delta S_1$ and $\Delta S_2$ respectively. Then:
questions.explanation: $\Delta S = q/T$ for the same q; since T$_1$ > T$_2$, dividing by the larger temperature gives the smaller entropy change, so $\Delta S_1 < \Delta S_2$.

questions.q: The reaction in which $\Delta H > \Delta U$ is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$, so $\Delta H > \Delta U$ requires $\Delta n_g > 0$; only the decomposition of CaCO3(s) increases moles of gas (0 to 1), giving $\Delta n_g = +1$.

questions.q: A reaction has both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ – ve. The rate of reaction
options: remains unaffected by change in temperature
cannot be predicted for change in temperature
questions.explanation: With $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ both negative, $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ becomes more negative (more favourable) as temperature decreases, so the reaction (and its effective rate of product formation) is favoured at lower temperature.

questions.q: If the bond energies of H$-$H, Br$-$Br and H$-$Br are 433, 192 and 364 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively, then $\Delta H\degree$ for the reaction : H$_2$(g) + Br$_2$(g) $\rightarrow$ 2HBr(g) is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Sigma$(bonds broken) $- \Sigma$(bonds formed) = (433+192) $-$ 2(364) = 625 $-$ 728 = $-103$ kJ.

questions.q: The correct statement regarding entropy is,
options: At absolute zero temperature, entropy of a perfectly crystalline solid is zero.
At absolute zero temperature, the entropy of a perfectly crystalline substance is +Ve.
At absolute zero temperature, the entropy of all crystalline substances is zero.
At 0 °C, the entropy of a perfect crystalline solid is zero.
questions.explanation: This is the third law of thermodynamics: the entropy of a perfectly crystalline solid is zero at absolute zero (0 K).

questions.q: In the reaction S + $\dfrac{3}{2}$O$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ SO$_3$ + 2x kJ and SO$_2$ + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ SO$_3$ + y kJ, heat of formation of SO$_2$ is
questions.explanation: By Hess's law, the direct path (S+O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_2$, releasing h) followed by (SO$_2$+½O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_3$, releasing y) must release the same total heat as the direct route S+3/2O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_3$ (releasing 2x); so h + y = 2x, giving the heat of formation of SO$_2$ as h = 2x − y. This question was awarded a grace mark by KEA.

questions.q:
The ratio of heats liberated at 298 K from the combustion of one kg of coke and by burning water gas obtained from kg of coke is

(Assume coke to be 100% carbon.)

(Given enthalpies of combustion of C to CO$_2$, CO to CO$_2$ and H$_2$ to H$_2$O as 393.5 kJ, 285 kJ, 285 kJ respectively all at 298 K.)
questions.explanation: Per mole of carbon, direct combustion releases 393.5 kJ, while water gas (1 mol CO + 1 mol H$_2$) on combustion releases 285+285 = 570 kJ; ratio = 393.5/570 ≈ 0.69:1. KEA awarded a grace mark, likely due to ambiguity in the printed enthalpy values.

questions.q: Conversion of oxygen into ozone is non-spontaneous at
questions.explanation: 3O$_2$ → 2O$_3$ has positive ΔH (endothermic) and negative ΔS (decrease in moles of gas), so ΔG = ΔH - TΔS is positive at all temperatures, making the conversion non-spontaneous at all temperatures.

questions.q: Given Thermochemical equation, 2H$_{2(g)}$ + O$_{2(g)}$ $\rightarrow$ 2H$_2$O$_{(l)}$; $\Delta$H = -571.6 kJ. Heat of decomposition of water is
questions.explanation: Formation of 2 mol water releases 571.6 kJ, so formation of 1 mol releases 285.8 kJ; decomposition of 1 mol water therefore requires +285.8 kJ.

questions.q: The process is spontaneous at the given temperature, if
options: $\Delta$H is +ve and $\Delta$S is equal to zero
questions.explanation: $\Delta$G = $\Delta$H - T$\Delta$S is always negative when $\Delta$H is negative and $\Delta$S is positive, so the process is spontaneous at all temperatures.

questions.q: The value of entropy of solar system is
questions.explanation: By the second law of thermodynamics, the entropy of an isolated system such as the (approximately isolated) solar system/universe keeps increasing.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant of a reaction is 0.008 at 298 K. The standard free energy change of the reaction at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: $\Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K=-8.314\times298\times\ln(0.008)\approx+11.96$ kJ (K<1 gives positive $\Delta G^\circ$).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The total entropy of the universe remains constant.
The total entropy of the universe is continuously decreasing.
The total energy of the universe is continuously decreasing.
The total energy of the universe remains constant.
questions.explanation: By the first law of thermodynamics (law of conservation of energy), the total energy of the universe remains constant.

questions.q: A gas expands from a volume of 1 m$^3$ to a volume of 2 m$^3$ against an external pressure of 10$^5$ Nm$^{-2}$. The work done by the gas will be
The amount of heat evolved when 500 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M $HCl$ is mixed with 200 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Moles $NaOH$ (limiting reagent) = 0.2×0.2 = 0.04 mol; using the standard enthalpy of neutralization of a strong acid-strong base (≈57.3 kJ/mol), heat evolved = 0.04×57.3 = 2.292 kJ.

questions.q: The enthalpy of vaporization of benzene is +35.3 kJ/mol at its boiling point of 80$^0$C. The entropy change in the transition of vapour to liquid at its boiling point is .............. [in J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$].
questions.explanation: $\Delta S=-\Delta H_{vap}/T=-35300/353\approx-100$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, since condensation is the reverse of vaporization.

questions.q: Based on the first law of thermodynamics, which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta U=q+w$ (w = work done on the system): for a cyclic process $\Delta U=0$, so $q=-w$; the other three statements contradict the first law under this convention.

questions.q: Enthalpy of vapourization of benzene is +35.3 kJ mol$^{-1}$ at its boiling point of 80$^0$C. The entropy change in the transition of the vapour to liquid at its boiling point [in JK$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$] is ........................
questions.explanation: $\Delta S_{vap} = \dfrac{35300}{353} = 100$ J K$^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$; condensation (vapour to liquid) is the reverse, so $\Delta S = -100$ J K$^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The amount of heat evolved when 500 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M $HCl$ is mixed with 200 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$ is .......................
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.05, moles NaOH = 0.04 (limiting). Heat evolved = 0.04 mol $\times$ 57.3 kJ/mol $\approx$ 2.292 kJ.

questions.q: Based on the first law of thermodynamics, which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta U = q + w$, for a cyclic process $\Delta U = 0$, so $q = -w$.

questions.q: The enthalpy of formation of NH$_3$ is $-46$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. The enthalpy change for the reaction: 2NH$_3$(g) $\longrightarrow$ N$_2$(g) + 3H$_2$(g) is
questions.explanation: Reversing and doubling the formation reaction gives $\Delta H$ = $-2\times(-46)$ = +92 kJ.

questions.q: For the reaction H$_2$O (l) $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$O(g) at 373 K and one atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: At the normal boiling point the liquid and vapour are in equilibrium, so $\Delta G=0$, which gives $\Delta H = T\Delta S$.
